# iliad-071 — renderings chosen for 11.804–848 (to be copied into conventions.md)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς φάτο, τῷ δ’ ἄρα θυμὸν ἐνὶ στήθεσσιν ὄρινε (11.804, masculine; Patroclus is the stirred man) | "So he spoke, and in him the heart in his breast he stirred," | "So he spoke, and he stirred the heart in Patroclus’ breast" | the table’s 4.208 row unchanged, with the name changed; the line here ends in a comma (the sentence runs into 805), so the unit is not the published one-line unit and the `l` is simply reused |
| βῆ δὲ θέειν (11.805) | "and went to run" | "set off running" | "ran" alone (drops βῆ), "hurried" |
| ἐπ’ Αἰακίδην Ἀχιλῆα (11.805) | "to the descendant of Aeacus, Achilles" | "to Achilles, descendant of Aeacus" | "son of Aeacus", "grandson" (the table’s Αἰακίδης "descendant of Aeacus") |
| Ὀδυσσῆος θείοιο (11.806) | "of divine Odysseus" | "of divine Odysseus" | "heavenly" (reserved for δῖος); follows the table’s 21.189 row |
| ἀγορή τε θέμις τε (11.807) | "assembly and custom" | "their assembly and their settled custom" | "justice", "law", "right" (the table keeps "custom" for θέμις, 2.73); a pair of nouns naming the army’s place of meeting |
| ἤην (11.808) | "was" | "had (their assembly …)" | the form is the Homeric imperfect of εἰμί, noted in the unit |
| ἐτετεύχατο βωμοί (11.808) | "had been built" (altars) | "had been built" | "had been made", "stood" |
| διογενὴς Εὐαιμονίδης (11.810) | "Zeus-sprung Euaemon’s-son" | "Zeus-born son of Euaemon" | follows the table’s διογενής pair and the patronymic as "Atreus’-son" / "son of" |
| σκάζων ἐκ πολέμου (11.811) | "limping from the war" | "limping from the war" | "hobbling", "lame" |
| νότιος ἱδρώς (11.811) | "wet sweat" | "wet sweat" | "moist", "clammy", "southern" (νότιος is not the south wind here) |
| αἷμα μέλαν κελάρυζε (11.812–813) | "dark blood gurgled" | "dark blood came gurgling out" | "black blood" (the table’s αἷμα κελαινόν / μέλαν "dark blood"), "welled", "spurted", "poured" |
| ἕλκος ἀργαλέον (11.812) | "wound, grievous" | "the grievous wound" | "painful", "cruel"; ἀργαλέος "grievous" |
| νόος ἔμπεδος (11.813) | "mind … firm" | "mind … firm" | "steady", "unshaken" (ἀστεμφής "unshaken"); ἔμπεδος "firm" as in the table’s φυλακὴ ἔμπεδος |
| ἆ δειλοί (11.816) | "Oh, miserable ones" | "Oh, you miserable …" | "Ah" / "Ah me" (reserved for ὢ πόποι), "cowards", "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος); follows the Odyssey table’s ἆ δειλοί (10.431) "Oh, miserable ones" / "Oh, you miserable men" and δειλοὶ βροτοί "miserable mortals" |
| Δαναῶν ἡγήτορες ἠδὲ μέδοντες (11.816) | "leaders and lords of the Danaans" | "the leaders and lords of the Danaans" | the table’s Ἀργείων ἡγήτορες ἠδὲ μέδοντες (2.79) with Δαναοί |
| ὣς ἄρ’ ἐμέλλετε … ἄσειν (11.817–818) | "so then you were destined … to glut" | "so it was to be, then, that … you would glut" | "were doomed", "were going to", "feed" (ἄσειν is "sate, glut", and the dogs are glutted with fat); follows the table’s ἔμελλον "destined" (5.686) |
| ταχέας κύνας ἀργέτι δημῷ (11.818) | "the swift dogs with white fat" | "the swift dogs … with your white fat" | "fleet", "bright fat", "shining fat" (ἀργής "bright, white"; the form ἀργέτι is epic) |
| ἀλλ’ ἄγε μοι τόδε εἰπέ (11.819) | "But come, tell me this" | "But come now, tell me this" | the Odyssey’s ἀλλ’ ἄγε μοι τόδε εἰπὲ καὶ ἀτρεκέως κατάλεξον row ("But come, tell me this" / "But come now, tell me this") |
| διοτρεφὲς Εὐρύπυλ’ ἥρως (11.819) | "Zeus-nurtured one, Eurypylus, hero" | same | the table’s διοτρεφές "Zeus-nurtured one"; ἥρως "hero" as a title (11.771) |
| ἤ ῥ’ ἔτι που σχήσουσι … ἦ ἤδη φθίσονται (11.820–821) | "whether still, I wonder, … will hold back … or already … will perish" | "will the Achaeans, I wonder, still hold … back, or will they already perish" | "I suppose", "perhaps" (που is "I wonder" in a question) |
| δουρὶ δαμέντες (11.821) | "with the spear subdued" | "overcome by the spear" | "tamed", "slain" (δάμνημι "overpower") |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύπυλος βεβλημένος ἀντίον ηὔδα (11.822, whole-line reply-formula) | "Him then in turn Eurypylus, struck, spoke, face to face:" | "Then the wounded Eurypylus spoke to him in turn, face to face:" | "answered" (reserved for ἀμείβετο); built on the table’s τὸν δ’ αὖτ’ Αἰνείας Τρώων ἀγὸς ἀντίον ηὔδα (5.217) and βεβλημένος "struck" / "wounded" (11.592) |
| οὐκέτι διογενὲς Πατρόκλεες ἄλκαρ Ἀχαιῶν ἔσσεται (11.823–824) | "No longer, Zeus-sprung Patroclus, a defence of the Achaeans will there be" | "There will be no defence for the Achaeans any longer, Zeus-born Patroclus" | "bulwark", "help" (ἄλκαρ "defence", 5.644) |
| κέαται βεβλημένοι οὐτάμενοί τε (11.826) | "lie, struck and wounded" | "lie … struck and wounded" | "hit", "pierced" (the pair of the table’s 11.657–661 row) |
| χερσὶν ὕπο Τρώων (11.827) | "under the hands of the Trojans" | "at the hands of the Trojans" | "by the Trojans" (loses χερσίν) |
| σθένος ὄρνυται αἰέν (11.827) | "the strength rises always" | "their strength is always rising" | "might" (reserved for ἀλκή / μένος); σθένος "strength" |
| σάωσον ἄγων ἐπὶ νῆα μέλαιναν (11.828) | "save, leading me to a black ship" | "save me, and take me to a black ship" | "dark ship", "my ship"; the table’s νηῦς μέλαινα "a black ship" |
| ἔκταμ’ ὀϊστόν (11.829) | "cut out the arrow" | "Cut the arrow out" | "pull out", "draw out" (ἐκτάμνω is "cut out") |
| ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ δ’ αἷμα κελαινὸν νίζ’ ὕδατι λιαρῷ (11.829–830 = 11.845–846, imperative then imperfect) | "from it the dark blood wash / he washed with warm water" | "wash the dark blood from it with warm water" / "he washed the dark blood from it with warm water" | "black blood" (the table’s αἷμα κελαινόν "dark blood"), "tepid", "lukewarm", "hot" (λιαρός "warm"; the table keeps "hot" for θερμός) |
| ἤπια φάρμακα … ἐσθλά (11.830–831) | "gentle drugs, good ones" | "gentle drugs, good ones" | "soothing", "kindly" (the table’s ἤπια φάρμακα, 4.218); ἐσθλός "good" |
| ἐπὶ … πάσσε (11.830) | "upon … sprinkle" | "sprinkle on" | "scatter", "apply" |
| τά σε προτί φασιν Ἀχιλλῆος δεδιδάχθαι (11.831) | "which they say you have been taught by Achilles" | "of the kind they say you have been taught by Achilles" | "learned from"; the perfect passive is kept |
| δικαιότατος Κενταύρων (11.832) | "most just of the Centaurs" | "the most just of the Centaurs" | "the most righteous", "the fairest" (δίκαιος "just"); Κένταυρος "Centaur" as in the table |
| ἰητροί … ἀμύμονος ἰητῆρος (11.833, 11.835) | "healers … a blameless healer" | "the healers … a blameless healer" | "doctors", "physicians"; ἰητήρ "healer", ἀμύμων "blameless" (+ note: the sense is not known) |
| ὀΐομαι … κεῖσθαι (11.834–836) | "I think … to lie" | "I think … lies" | "suppose", "believe" |
| μένει ὀξὺν Ἄρηα (11.836) | "awaits … sharp Ares" | "waits … for the Trojans’ keen battle" | the table’s ὀξὺν Ἄρηα "sharp Ares" / "keen battle" (2.440) unchanged |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε Μενοιτίου ἄλκιμος υἱός (11.837, whole-line reply-formula) | "Him then in turn addressed Menoetius’ sturdy son:" | "Then Menoetius’ sturdy son spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); the table’s τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε (9.114) with the 11.605 name-epithet row |
| πῶς τὰρ ἔοι τάδε ἔργα; (11.838) | "How then might these deeds be?" | "How then could these matters be so?" | "How can these things be?" (a remembered biblical phrase), "How could this be?", "What are we to make of this?" (the note explains τὰρ as τ’ ἄρ, as at 1.8) |
| τί ῥέξομεν; (11.838) | "What shall we do" | "What are we to do" | "What can we do" (a deliberative future, not ability) |
| ἔρχομαι ὄφρ’ … μῦθον ἐνίσπω (11.839) | "I am going so that … the word I may tell" | "I am on my way so that I may tell … the word" | "to bring the message", "deliver" (ἐνίσπω is "tell") |
| Ἀχιλῆϊ δαΐφρονι (11.839) | "wise-minded Achilles" | "wise-hearted Achilles" (+ note: "wise" or "fierce" disputed) | the table’s δαΐφρων "wise-minded" / "wise-hearted"; "warlike" |
| ὃν Νέστωρ ἐπέτελλε Γερήνιος οὖρος Ἀχαιῶν (11.840) | "which Nestor enjoined, the Gerenian, warden of the Achaeans" | "that Nestor the Gerenian, warden of the Achaeans, gave instructions for" | "charged" (avoided at 5.198), "bulwark" (that is ἕρκος); the table’s ἐπέτελλε (5.198) and οὖρος Ἀχαιῶν (3.411) |
| ἀλλ’ οὐδ’ ὧς περ σεῖο μεθήσω τειρομένοιο (11.841) | "but not even so will I let you go, being worn down" | "But even so I will not leave you, worn down as you are" | "abandon" (stronger than μεθίημι), "distressed" (the table keeps "worn down" for τείρω, 5.352) |
| ἦ, καὶ ὑπὸ στέρνοιο λαβὼν ἄγε ποιμένα λαῶν (11.842) | "He spoke, and taking him under the breast he led the shepherd of the people" | "So he said, and, taking him under the breast, he led the shepherd of the people" | "under the chest" (στῆθος keeps "chest"; στέρνον "breast", as in the table’s 4.528 row), "supporting him", "by the arm"; the table’s ἦ καί (1.219) and ποιμένα λαῶν "shepherd of the people" |
| ἐς κλισίην (11.843) | "to the hut" | "to the hut" | "tent", "shelter" |
| θεράπων … ὑπέχευε βοείας (11.843) | "the attendant … spread oxhides underneath" | "the attendant … spread oxhides underneath" | "servant" (reserved for δμῶς), "squire"; θεράπων "attendant" (2.110), βοείη "oxhide" (as the table’s κνημῖδες βοείαι "oxhide greaves") |
| ἐκτανύσας (11.844) | "having stretched him out" | "stretched him out" | "laid him down" |
| τάμνε μαχαίρῃ (11.844) | "cut with a knife" | "cut … with a knife" | "sword", "dagger", "blade" (μάχαιρα is a large knife, not a sword) |
| ὀξὺ βέλος περιπευκές (11.844–845) | "the sharp shaft, very sharp" | "the very sharp shaft" (+ note: sense of περιπευκές not certain) | "keen", "pointed" (kept for ἐχεπευκής); ὀξὺ βέλος "the sharp shaft" (4.185) with περι- "very" as in περικαλλής |
| ῥίζαν πικρήν (11.846) | "a bitter root" | "a bitter root" | "sharp root" (ὀξύς), "harsh" |
| διατρίψας (11.847) | "having rubbed it through" | "after rubbing it between his hands" | "crushing", "grinding" (each decides the means) |
| ὀδυνήφατον (11.847) | "pain-slaying" | "pain-killing" (+ note: ὀδύνη "pain" + a root meaning "kill", not certain) | "soothing", "pain-relieving"; the table’s ὀδυνήφατα φάρμακα (5.401) |
| ἔσχ’ ὀδύνας (11.847–848) | "the pains checked" | "checked all his pains" | "stopped", "ended", "held back" (each decides the cure is complete) |
| τὸ μὲν ἕλκος ἐτέρσετο, παύσατο δ’ αἷμα (11.848) | "the wound dried, and the blood ceased" | "the wound dried up, and the blood stopped" | "closed", "healed" (the Greek says only "dried"), "clotted" |
